## Hands-on 1 – The setup check {#hands-on-1-get-yourself-running .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 1 – the setup check.** Get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you.

- **Browser lab:** the page has finished loading, the cell of Task 1 runs, and the panel has 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years
- **Workspace, if you installed it:** your IDE opens the folder, `source("R/check_setup.R")` reports no failure, and the report renders once
- While R loads, the warm-up below Task 1 sorts four scenarios into the three Rs
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Take the time you need, **into the break** if necessary. Type a green circle in the chat when you are through, and **STUCK** if you need me.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
If the workspace will not cooperate, do not fight it: the browser lab holds every task of the day.
:::

::: notes
Your turn, and this first task is deliberately not intellectual. The job is to get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. In the browser lab, wait until the page has finished loading, press Run Code on the cell of Task 1, and check that the panel has two hundred and seventy rows, twenty-seven countries and ten years. While you wait, the warm-up below it asks you to sort four scenarios into the three Rs. If you installed the workspace, open its folder in your IDE, run the check script and render the report once. Take the time you need, into the break if you have to. Green circle in the chat when you are through, STUCK if you need me. And if the workspace will not cooperate, leave it for later, because the browser lab holds every task of the day.
:::
